mainTopic: How far suspicion reaches: רבא's penalty on a cheating butcher, the משנה on suspicion about שביעית, מעשרות and טהרות, and who disagrees with it
overview: This amud opens with a story. A butcher sold forbidden fat as permitted fat, and רבא banned him from selling even nuts. רב פפא asks whether this follows רבי יהודה, who would ban even water and salt. רבא answers that he follows רבי שמעון, because the butcher used nuts to bribe children into bringing him the forbidden fat. A new משנה then teaches that suspicion on שביעית and suspicion on מעשרות do not carry over to each other. Suspicion on either one does carry over to טהרות, but not the reverse. A suspected person may not judge or testify on his matter. The גמרא explains each clause: מעשר must be eaten inside ירושלים, שביעית cannot be redeemed, and Torah laws are heavier than rabbinic ones. It then settles a contradiction from a ברייתא with two different answers. Finally, רבי יוחנן says the משנה follows רבי עקיבא, and two versions identify the disagreeing חכמים as רבי יהודה or רבי מאיר. A dispute between two students about these versions begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא penalizes a butcher who sold forbidden fat
steps.stepSummary: A butcher sold forbidden thigh-area fat as permitted intestinal fat, and רבא banned him from selling even nuts.
steps.simpleTranslation: [A butcher sold] fat of the thigh area as if it were fat of the intestines. רבא penalized him and did not let him sell even nuts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case. A butcher cheated with forbidden fat, and רבא fined him with a ban that reached even nuts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה had a מחלוקת. רבי יהודה says a suspected person is not trusted on anything. רבי שמעון says he is only distrusted on things connected to his sin. Banning nuts, which seem to have nothing to do with fat, looks like רבי יהודה's view, and that sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Fat of the thigh/kidney area, which is forbidden חֵלֶב
Fat of the intestines, which is permitted
He penalized him (from קְנָס, a fine or penalty)

phrases.english: [One who sold] fat of the thigh area as fat of the intestines,
phrases.notes: The first word of the story picks up from the previous page: he sold forbidden fat as permitted fat.

phrases.english: Rava penalized him
[forbidding him] to sell even nuts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the previous משנה's מחלוקת about suspected people to a real case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A butcher who sold forbidden fat as permitted fat is penalized and may not sell even nuts.

steps.title: רב פפא asks which opinion רבא is following
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא argues that banning nuts must follow רבי יהודה. But then the ban should go even further, to water and salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: Whose opinion are you following? רבי יהודה? If you follow רבי יהודה, then he should be banned even from selling water and salt!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges רבא's ruling. He says it does not match either opinion cleanly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nuts have no obvious link to fat, so the ban seems to follow רבי יהודה's wide view. But רבי יהודה bans even water and salt. So if רבא follows him, why stop at nuts? The ruling looks like a half-way position.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? (Whose opinion is this?)
Water and salt: the extreme example in רבי יהודה's view

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava:
According to whom? According to Rabbi Yehuda?
If according to Rabbi Yehuda,
then even water and salt too [should be banned]!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְרָבָא: כְּמַאן? כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in step 1.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling is too broad for רבי שמעון and too narrow for רבי יהודה, so it fits neither.

steps.title: רבא explains that the nuts were the tool of the crime
steps.stepSummary: רבא follows רבי שמעון. The nuts are directly tied to the sin, because the butcher used them to bribe children into bringing him forbidden fat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, I follow רבי שמעון, and we are penalizing him on matters tied to the prohibition itself. Children are usually drawn to nuts. This man would go and mislead the butchers' children and tempt them with nuts. They would bring him forbidden thigh fat, and he would sell it as permitted intestinal fat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רב פפא. The ban on nuts is not a wide ban at all, because the nuts were part of how he did the cheating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון only distrusts a suspected person in matters connected to his sin. רבא shows that nuts were connected: they were the bribe used to get the forbidden fat. So the ban stays inside רבי שמעון's limits, and water and salt are still allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually: introduces the answer that keeps the original position
The prohibition itself (the very sin he committed)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא follows רבי שמעון. The penalty can reach things that look unrelated, such as nuts, if they were actually used to commit the sin.

phrases.english: Really, [it follows] Rabbi Shimon,
and we are penalizing him regarding the prohibition itself.
Ordinary children are enticed by nuts,
and he would go and mislead the butchers' children,
and entice them with nuts,
and they would bring him fat of the thigh area,
and he would sell it as fat of the intestines.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, וּבְאִיסּוּרָא דְּגוּפֵיהּ קָנְסִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge from step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the nuts turn out to be directly connected to the sin.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Nuts seemed unrelated to fat, so banning them looked like רבי יהודה's wide view.
steps.terutzMaskana: Nuts were the bribe used to get the forbidden fat, so banning them fits רבי שמעון.

steps.title: משנה: Suspicion on one area does not always carry over to another
steps.stepSummary: Suspicion on שביעית and suspicion on מעשרות do not carry over to each other. Suspicion on either one does carry over to טהרות, but not in the other direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone suspected about שביעית is not suspected about מעשרות. Someone suspected about מעשרות is not suspected about שביעית. Someone suspected about either of these is suspected about טהרות. But some people are suspected about טהרות and are not suspected about either of the others.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It maps out which kinds of suspicion spread to other areas and which do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person treats different מצוות as lighter or heavier. Neglecting one area does not prove he neglects another. But טהרות is seen as lighter than both שביעית and מעשרות. So whoever is lax with either of the heavier ones is surely lax with טהרות, while being lax with טהרות proves nothing about the heavier ones.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the text marks it with the short form מַתְנִי׳)
The seventh year (שמיטה) and the laws of its produce
Ritual purity: here, selling impure food as if it were pure

steps.confusionAlert: The direction matters here. Suspicion on שביעית or מעשרות spreads to טהרות. Suspicion on טהרות does not spread back to them.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who is suspected regarding the Sabbatical Year
is not suspected regarding tithes;
one who is suspected regarding tithes
is not suspected regarding the Sabbatical Year.
One who is suspected regarding this or that
is suspected regarding ritual purity;
but there is one who is suspected regarding ritual purity

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ חָשׁוּד לֹא עַל זֶה וְלֹא עַל זֶה.
phrases.english: and is not suspected regarding either this or that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It continues the general theme of how far suspicion reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suspicion on שביעית and on מעשרות do not carry over to each other. Either one carries over to טהרות, but טהרות does not carry over to them.

steps.title: משנה's general rule: A suspected person cannot judge or testify on that matter
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sums up: whoever is suspected on a matter may not judge it or testify about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: someone suspected about a matter may not judge it and may not testify about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with a general principle that applies to every kind of suspicion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Beyond the question of buying food from him, suspicion also takes away a person's legal reliability in that same area. He cannot serve as a judge or as a witness on the matter he is suspected about.

keyTerms.meaning: Judges it (serves as a judge on that matter)

steps.whatToRemember: Suspicion is limited to its own area. Within that area, the person is distrusted for business, for judging, and for testimony.

phrases.english: This is the principle:
one who is suspected regarding a matter
may neither judge it nor testify about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the משנה's cases in step 4 with a general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A suspected person may not judge or testify on the matter he is suspected about.

steps.title: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why someone suspected on שביעית is not suspected on מעשרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the logic behind the משנה's first ruling. This line sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first it seems that someone who ignores one agricultural law would ignore another. The גמרא wants to know what makes מעשר feel different to this person.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion (the text marks it with the short form גְּמָ׳)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the first ruling in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why suspicion on שביעית does not carry over to מעשרות.

steps.title: Tithes feel stricter because they must be eaten inside ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: שביעית produce has no requirement to be eaten inside the wall of ירושלים. מעשר שני must be eaten inside the wall, so this person takes it more seriously.
steps.simpleTranslation: שביעית does not require the wall of ירושלים. With מעשר, since it requires the wall, it is stricter in his eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. מעשר feels more serious to people because it has a special rule tying it to ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני may only be eaten inside the walls of ירושלים, and that special status makes it feel holier and stricter. שביעית produce has no such rule. So a person might treat שביעית lightly and still be careful with מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Wall: the walls of ירושלים, inside which מעשר שני must be eaten
Second tithe, which is eaten in ירושלים
It is stringent / serious in his eyes

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the גמרא measures suspicion by how serious each מצוה feels to the person, not only by its formal legal weight.

phrases.english: The Sabbatical Year does not require the wall [of Jerusalem];
tithe, since it requires the wall,
is stringent in his eyes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מעשר requires eating inside the wall of ירושלים, so it feels stricter than שביעית. Laxity on שביעית therefore does not prove laxity on מעשר.

steps.title: Why is someone suspected on מעשר still trusted on שביעית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next clause, that one suspected on מעשר is not suspected on שביעית, and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one who is suspected on tithes is not suspected on שביעית. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next piece of the משנה and asks why it is true. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 asked about one direction: suspected on שביעית but trusted on מעשר. Now the גמרא asks about the reverse direction. We need a separate reason for why a person who is careless with מעשר would still be careful with שביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is suspected of not keeping a halacha
Tithe, a portion of produce that must be separated

phrases.english: The one suspected regarding tithes.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה: he is not suspected on שביעית.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 6, now asking about the opposite direction.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why suspicion on מעשר does not carry over to שביעית.

steps.title: מעשר can be redeemed, שביעית produce cannot
steps.stepSummary: מעשר has a way out through redemption, so he treats it lightly. שביעית produce stays forbidden with no redemption, so he treats it seriously.
steps.simpleTranslation: Tithes can be redeemed. But שביעית produce stays forbidden to him and cannot be redeemed, so he treats it as more serious.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Because שביעית has no redemption option, this person treats it more strictly than מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני can be redeemed for money, which makes the prohibition feel flexible. Someone who is lax about it may tell himself it can be fixed. שביעית has no such fix, so even this person takes it seriously and stays trustworthy on it.

keyTerms.meaning: Redemption, exchanging holy produce for money
It is serious or strict in his eyes

phrases.english: Tithe has redemption,
phrases.notes: So a person may treat it lightly.

phrases.english: Sabbatical produce, since it is forbidden to him
and it has no redemption, it is serious to him.

steps.whatToRemember: Each direction has its own reason. שביעית→מעשר: מעשר must be eaten inside the walls of ירושלים. מעשר→שביעית: שביעית cannot be redeemed.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שביעית has no redemption, so it feels more serious than מעשר, which can be redeemed.

steps.title: Suspected on a Torah law means suspected on a rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: Someone suspected on שביעית or on מעשר is also suspected on טהרות. If he breaks Torah law, he will surely break rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said that one suspected on either of these is suspected on purity. Since he is suspected on Torah law, all the more so on rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the משנה's next clause. Someone who is careless with Torah-level laws will surely be careless with a rabbinic-level law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שביעית and מעשר are treated here as Torah laws. טהרות, meaning eating ordinary food in purity, is only rabbinic. So suspicion flows downward from the stricter category to the lighter one through a simple כל שכן.

keyTerms.meaning: On this or on that, meaning שביעית or מעשר

phrases.english: One suspected on this or on that.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה: he is suspected on טהרות.

phrases.english: Since he is suspected on Torah law,
all the more so on rabbinic law.

steps.confusionAlert: In this sugya, טהרות means eating ordinary food in a state of purity. That is a rabbinic practice, not a Torah law. This is why it counts as the lighter category here.
steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דַּחֲשִׁיד אַדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן אַדְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suspicion on Torah-level laws (שביעית, מעשר) carries over to rabbinic-level טהרות by כל שכן.

steps.title: Why isn't someone suspected on טהרות suspected on שביעית and מעשר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: some people are suspected on טהרות but not on שביעית or מעשר. It asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: there are those suspected on purity who are not suspected on the others. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last clause of the משנה and asks for its reason. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the גמרא asks about the reverse direction of step 10. Why doesn't suspicion flow upward from טהרות to שביעית and מעשר?

keyTerms.meaning: Purity laws, here eating ordinary food in purity
And there is one who is suspected

phrases.english: And there is one suspected on purity items.
phrases.notes: Who is not suspected on שביעית or מעשר.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ חָשׁוּד עַל הַטְּהָרוֹת. מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the opposite direction of step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why suspicion on טהרות does not carry over to שביעית and מעשר.

steps.title: Breaking a rabbinic law doesn't mean breaking a Torah law
steps.stepSummary: He may be careless with rabbinic laws, but that does not show he is careless with Torah laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, he is suspected on rabbinic law, but he is not suspected on Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers simply. Being lax with a lighter, rabbinic law does not prove someone is lax with a stricter, Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כל שכן only works in one direction, from heavier to lighter. Someone who is careless about a rabbinic practice may still respect Torah prohibitions.

phrases.english: Granted, he is suspected on rabbinic law,
but on Torah law he is not suspected.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Suspicion on a lighter rabbinic law does not carry over to heavier Torah laws.

steps.title: A ברייתא links trust on טהרות with trust on שביעית
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says one trusted on טהרות is trusted on שביעית. That implies one suspected on טהרות is suspected on שביעית, which contradicts the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They contrasted it with a ברייתא: one trusted on purity is trusted on שביעית. So if he is suspected on purity, he is suspected on שביעית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict the משנה. It reads the ברייתא to mean that suspicion on purity also makes a person suspected on שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא ties the two areas together: trust in one goes with trust in the other. The גמרא infers the flip side, that suspicion on טהרות means suspicion on שביעית. That directly clashes with the משנה and with the reasoning of step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted it with a source, introducing a contradiction

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:

phrases.aramaic: נֶאֱמָן עַל הַטְּהָרוֹת — נֶאֱמָן עַל שְׁבִיעִית,
phrases.english: one trusted on purity items is trusted on שביעית,
which implies: if suspected, he is suspected!
phrases.notes: The inference the גמרא draws from the ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה clause explained in steps 11 and 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that one suspected on טהרות is not suspected on שביעית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא links trust on טהרות to trust on שביעית. The inference is that suspicion on one means suspicion on the other.

steps.title: The משנה is about a person seen keeping the laws in private
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעי explains that the משנה is speaking of someone we have seen observing שביעית and מעשר carefully in his own home.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעי said: the משנה is talking about a case where we saw him acting carefully in private, inside his home.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילעי resolves the contradiction by limiting the משנה to a special case. In that case we have direct evidence that the person keeps שביעית and מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the ברייתא's rule holds: suspicion on טהרות brings suspicion on שביעית. The משנה describes an exception, a person seen being careful about שביעית and מעשר in private. That direct evidence of his care outweighs his laxness on purity.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who gives the answer

phrases.english: Rabbi Ilai said:
The mishna is where we saw him
conducting himself carefully in private, within his home.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אילעי, suspicion on טהרות normally does carry over to שביעית, as the ברייתא says. The משנה is the exception: a person seen keeping these laws privately at home. The next step gives a different answer that reverses which source is the exception.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of step 13 by limiting the case in the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the משנה to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to state a general rule that one suspected on טהרות is trusted on שביעית.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה applies only where he was seen keeping שביעית and מעשר privately at home. Otherwise the ברייתא's link holds.

steps.title: A second answer: he once repented on both, then slipped on one
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי ברבי ישמעאל answers the contradiction a different way. The ברייתא is about a man who was suspected on both areas, publicly committed to keep both, and then was suspected again on one. Because he broke his promise on one, he is suspected on the other too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי ברבי ישמעאל said: The ברייתא is talking about a case where a man was suspected on both (טהרות and שביעית). He came before the חכמים and accepted on himself to keep both. Afterwards he was suspected again on one of them. In that case we say: since he is suspected on this one, he is also suspected on the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the contradiction from Step 13. This answer is about the ברייתא, which said that one who is not trusted on טהרות is not trusted on שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, being lax on טהרות, which is rabbinic, does not show that a person is lax on שביעית, which is Torah law. That is the משנה's rule. But this man promised the חכמים to keep both together and then broke his promise on one. That shows his word on either area cannot be relied on, so the ברייתא's ruling applies only to this special case.

keyTerms.meaning: He accepted upon himself (he committed in front of the חכמים)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the contradiction. In רבי אילעי's answer, the משנה is about a man we saw keeping שביעית and מעשר carefully. In רבי ינאי's answer, the ברייתא is about a man who repented on both and then slipped on one.
steps.confusionAlert: Notice which source each answer explains. רבי אילעי explained the case in the משנה. רבי ינאי explains the case in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai son of Rabbi Yishmael said:
For example, where he was suspected on both of them,
and he came before the Rabbis
and accepted upon himself to keep both of them,
and afterward he was suspected again on one of them,
where we say: since he is suspected on this one —
he is suspected on the other one as well.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יַנַּאי בְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אָמַר: כְּגוֹן דַּהֲוָה חֲשִׁיד לְתַרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a second answer to the קשיא in Step 13, offered next to רבי אילעי's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ברייתא to a special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to teach, as a general rule, that anyone suspected on טהרות is suspected on שביעית.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only about someone who promised to keep both and then broke his promise on one. In general, the משנה's rule stands.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי עקיבא; חכמים disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the משנה's rule (suspected on שביעית does not mean suspected on מעשר) is the view of רבי עקיבא. חכמים hold that one suspected on שביעית is suspected on מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This ruling is the opinion of רבי עקיבא, the author of unnamed משניות. But חכמים say: one who is suspected on שביעית is suspected on מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the opening line of the משנה. It shows that this ruling is a disputed opinion, not everyone's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats שביעית and מעשר as separate, so being lax in one does not prove laxness in the other. רבי יוחנן tells us that this is רבי עקיבא's view. Other חכמים link the two: someone careless about שביעית is also suspected about מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'unnamed one.' Unnamed משניות usually follow רבי עקיבא's views.
The seventh (Sabbatical) year and the laws of its produce
The Sages (here, the opinion that disagrees)

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes how we read the משנה. Its ruling is one side of a מחלוקת, not a universal rule.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
This is the statement of Rabbi Akiva, the unattributed one,
but the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: חָשׁוּד עַל הַשְּׁבִיעִית — חָשׁוּד עַל הַמַּעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.english: one suspected on the Sabbatical Year is suspected on tithes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סְתִימְתָּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This starts a new topic. It goes back to the first clause of the משנה and names who holds it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה follows רבי עקיבא. According to חכמים, one suspected on שביעית is suspected on מעשר.

steps.title: Who are these חכמים? רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who these חכמים are and answers: רבי יהודה. In his area, שביעית was treated very strictly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are these חכמים? It is רבי יהודה. In רבי יהודה's place, people treated שביעית as very serious.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא is the 'חכמים' of רבי יוחנן's statement. It answers right away: רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason comes from local practice. Where רבי יהודה lived, שביעית was taken more seriously than מעשר. So a person who was lax even with שביעית, the stricter law there, would surely be lax with מעשר.

phrases.english: Who are the Rabbis? Rabbi Yehuda,
for in the locale of Rabbi Yehuda
the Sabbatical Year was stringent for them,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This names the 'חכמים' of Step 16 and explains their reasoning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא is the 'חכמים' who links שביעית to מעשר?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is רבי יהודה, because in his area שביעית was treated as especially strict.

steps.title: A story showing how seriously שביעית was taken
steps.stepSummary: In רבי יהודה's area, if someone insulted another by calling him 'a convert, son of a convert,' the man would answer: 'At least I don't eat שביעית produce like you!' This shows that eating שביעית produce was considered shameful there.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who would call his friend 'a convert, son of a convert.' The friend would answer him: 'I deserve a blessing, because I don't eat שביעית produce like you do.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real-life example to prove that שביעית was treated very strictly in רבי יהודה's area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man answered an insult with a stronger insult: 'you eat שביעית produce.' That shows breaking שביעית was seen there as a worse disgrace than a family-background insult. This supports the claim in Step 17 that שביעית was the stricter law in that place.

keyTerms.meaning: A convert, son of a female convert (used here as an insult)
May a blessing come to me; I deserve credit

phrases.english: as that certain person who would call his fellow
'A convert, son of a female convert,'
he said to him: A blessing should come to me
for I do not eat Sabbatical Year produce like you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This proves the claim in Step 17 that שביעית was treated strictly in רבי יהודה's area.
steps.raayaObject: That שביעית was חמירא (treated especially strictly) in רבי יהודה's locale
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story of a local insult and the reply it got

steps.title: Another version: חכמים say suspected on מעשר means suspected on שביעית
steps.stepSummary: A second version of רבי יוחנן's statement reverses the direction. According to חכמים, one suspected on מעשר is suspected on שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say a different version: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This is the opinion of רבי עקיבא, the author of unnamed משניות. But חכמים say: one who is suspected on מעשר is suspected on שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רבי יוחנן's teaching. In this version, חכמים argue on the משנה's second clause instead of the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, חכמים linked שביעית to מעשר. Here the link goes the other way: from מעשר to שביעית. Both versions agree that the משנה follows רבי עקיבא. They differ only on which direction חכמים disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say (introduces an alternate version)

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the direction carefully. Version 1: suspected on שביעית means suspected on מעשר. Version 2: suspected on מעשר means suspected on שביעית.

phrases.english: There are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
This is the statement of Rabbi Akiva, the unattributed one,
but the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: חָשׁוּד עַל הַמַּעֲשֵׂר חָשׁוּד עַל הַשְּׁבִיעִית.
phrases.english: one suspected on tithes is suspected on the Sabbatical Year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is an alternate version of Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to חכמים, one suspected on מעשר is suspected on שביעית.

steps.title: In this version, חכמים is רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: In the second version, חכמים is רבי מאיר. He holds that someone suspected on one matter is suspected on the entire Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who are these חכמים? It is רבי מאיר, who says: one who is suspected on one thing is suspected on the whole Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies the 'חכמים' of the second version as רבי מאיר and gives his general rule. This closes the second version. The next step shows that the two versions reflect a real dispute between two students.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר does not need a special reason, such as a local custom, to link the two areas. In his view, anyone who knowingly breaks one law cannot be trusted on any law. So naturally, someone suspected on מעשר is suspected on שביעית.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה (רבי עקיבא) keeps שביעית and מעשר separate. Version 1: רבי יהודה says suspected on שביעית means suspected on מעשר, because of local strictness. Version 2: רבי מאיר says suspected on מעשר means suspected on שביעית, because someone suspected on one thing is suspected on the whole Torah.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי מאיר's broad rule, 'suspected on one thing is suspected on the whole Torah,' is a well-known position. It appears in other places that discuss trustworthiness.

phrases.english: And who are the Rabbis?
It is Rabbi Meir, who says:
one suspected on one matter
is suspected on the entire Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This names the 'חכמים' of the alternate version in Step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא is the 'חכמים' in the second version?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is רבי מאיר, who holds that one suspected on one matter is suspected on the whole Torah.

steps.title: Two students argue over how to report the view of חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names the two אמוראים who disagreed about the view of חכמים. They were either רבי יונה and רבי ירמיה, students of רבי זעירא, or רבי יונה and רבי זעירא, students of רבי יוחנן. It then begins the first opinion: 'But חכמים say one suspected on שביעית...'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונה and רבי ירמיה, students of רבי זעירא (and some say it was רבי יונה and רבי זעירא, students of רבי יוחנן), disagreed. One said: 'But חכמים say: one who is suspected on שביעית...' (the sentence continues on the next amud).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a dispute between two אמוראים to explain the two versions of רבי יוחנן's statement we just saw. It names who argued and starts quoting the first opinion. The rest of that opinion comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 16 and 19 gave two opposite directions for the view of חכמים. Here we learn that these are not just two copies of one tradition: two named אמוראים actually disagreed. The first opinion opens with the version from Step 16, that suspicion on שביעית leads to suspicion on מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: and some say. Introduces a different tradition about who said something.
one said. Opens the first side of a dispute between two people.
but the Sages say. The language of רבי יוחנן's statement, quoted here as the disputed line.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי זעירא shows up in both versions but in different roles. In the first version he is the teacher of the two who argued. In the second version he is himself one of the two who argued, and their teacher is רבי יוחנן.
